note: Release candidate 1 of the judge-facing cut, narrated. Authored: this is the one file under rc1/ a human writes. Holds are DERIVED from measured narration duration plus lead-in and tail, never hand-set, so a re-generated narration cannot leave a stale hold behind. Every visual is a frozen artifact produced by HAC-324, HAC-330, HAC-334, HAC-335, HAC-343 or HAC-350; this file selects and orders them and owns no facts.

narrationVoice.why: Calm, technically credible, conversational engineering register. Speed 1.05: once the lines were shortened for the Take 0.1 cold read they carried less internal pause, and 1.15 pushed the aggregate read to 158 wpm. Acronyms are written plainly (ADK, AI) rather than dotted; dotted forms cost roughly 30% in pace on this voice.

orderingNote: Single proof-class reset. All controlled-local and controlled-evaluation material precedes B05; all Google Cloud material follows it. The brief's section 5 spine placed Proof of Action at 0:45 and the four-strategy result at 2:00, which would cross the proof-class boundary three times. HAC-336's film gate refuses class-B material before the reset and class-A material after it, and AGENTS.md forbids weakening a gate. One reset is also the stronger answer to the section 12 reviewer question about whether a judge could conclude the controlled experiment ran on Google Cloud.

proofClasses.A: Controlled local experiment (HAC-330). Deterministic, local. No cloud runtime, no receipt, no protected target, no observer.
proofClasses.EVAL: Controlled local evaluation (HAC-343). Bounded sixteen-scenario corpus, exhaustively enumerated.
proofClasses.transition: Proof-class reset. Asserts only that nothing crosses.
proofClasses.B: Google Cloud participation (HAC-324 authoritative filmed run).
proofClasses.bounds: Claim boundary. States what is not claimed.
proofClasses.close: Close. Restates the thesis and where to verify it.

editorialTrim.why: HAC-350's final second is its own INTERLOCK end card. Inside that package it closes a standalone 30-second piece; dropped into this film it lands a brand card at 0:29 — a premature ending beat, and a duplicate of RC1's own closing card at R17. The trim removes only that card. Scene S8 (evidence ablation) settles at 29.0, so no evidence, figure or scene is shortened.

source.why: Devpost scores Proof of Action on an UNEDITED LIVE EXECUTION of the agent performing its task, and weights Demo & Production Readiness at 30% of Stage Two. The four frozen captures this beat replaces are real evidence of a real run, but they are stills: they ask a judge to trust that the screenshots came from something that happened, rather than showing it happen.

captureRules: One take. No cuts, splices, or B-roll inside the segment; editorial cuts only at its boundaries.
No cockpit, diagram or animation inside the segment - those explain it afterwards, they do not stand in for it.
If uniformly accelerated, the speed change is labelled visibly on the frame.
A persistent on-frame label reads LIVE UNEDITED - CLOUD RUN, and the run id appears once the run completes.

capture.why: Tail only. The recording opens on the prompt and the command, so nothing is removed from the head; the interior is untouched - no cut, no splice, no speed change. Devpost allows editorial cuts before and after a continuous proof segment, not inside one.
capture.marksNote: Within 0.06s of the planned marks, so the narration authored against the plan needed no re-timing. Every line still lands after the screen event it names.
capture.speedChange: none. Devpost permits a uniformly accelerated genuine run with disclosure; at 45s this take does not need one, so none was applied.

source.captureNote: Live take recorded 2026-08-31 19:34 local, run duration 45.07s per the script's own elapsed labels. captionPolicy.note: Take 0.1 cold read: rapid subtitle turnover competed with the visuals. Cues are wider and fewer, and a line is authored short enough to be one or two cues rather than four. Where the spoken and captioned forms differ the caption is the more precise record, printing tokens exactly (ALLOW_PARALLEL, EXECUTED, OBSERVED, gemini-3.5-flash) where the voice reads them as natural language.
captionPolicy.turnoverNote: Take 0.1 measured 12.8 cues/min at 4.02s mean. The ceiling is 11.0 rather than something lower because 33 narration lines across 3:38 put a hard floor of 9.1 cues/min at one cue per line: a stricter number could only be met by deleting propositions, not by editing. The reading load actually fell through two other levers - speech density 86.2% -> 67%, and a caption that now holds still through the gap after a short line instead of blanking.

attentionPolicy.note: Narration leads; the screen keeps the evidence. Three devices, all derived rather than eyeballed.
attentionPolicy.lead: A beat opens with lead-in silence before its first line, so the frame arrives before the voice does.
attentionPolicy.gap: A negative atSeconds is a GAP after the previous line, not an offset from the beat start. Between waves of narration the caption track is empty, so explanatory text is not changing while the viewer inspects a diagram or a measured result.
attentionPolicy.settle: tailSecondsOverride is the settle: the frame holds after the last line with nothing new to read, long enough for the narrated proposition to resolve. The densest boards (R03 four-strategy, R04 ablation) and the JSON evidence frame (R09) carry the longest settles, because that is where the cold read lost the argument.

audioOnlyDeicticWaiverReasons.N14: "Separately, here's the system running on Google Cloud." - "here's" is idiomatic spoken English introducing a topic, not a pointer at the frame; it parses with no picture. It is also the canonical proof-class reset line fixed by section 2 of the RC1 brief, so rewording it to satisfy a lint would break a requirement to satisfy a heuristic.

proofOfActionPolicy.note: The Google Cloud act must contain one unmistakably continuous live execution. Frozen captures may corroborate it; they may not substitute for it.
proofOfActionPolicy.requirement: Devpost Stage Two, Demo & Production Readiness (30%): Proof of Action asks whether the video shows an unedited, live execution of the agent performing its task. The rules separately require the video to demonstrate the backend running on Google Cloud.
proofOfActionPolicy.hierarchy: see it happen -> understand the receipt -> inspect the evidence

pronunciationNotes.invalid: Never send the bare word "invalid" to the synthesiser. It was read as the noun (IN-va-lid) rather than the adjective (in-VAL-id). Spoken lines say "unsafe outcomes"; captions keep "invalid", which is the frozen board's own label.
pronunciationNotes.run id: The synthesiser read the bare token "id" as the contraction "I'd". Fixed with a synthesis-only alias in pronunciationAliases rather than by rewriting the spoken line: "run id" is the canonical term the caption prints, and spelling it "eye dee" in cut-rc1.json would add a token to the spoken form that the caption does not have, failing CAP-precision-LV5. The alias is applied to the text sent to ElevenLabs and to the per-line cache key, so only the affected line re-synthesises.
